arguments.summary: A credential compromise occurred on host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) belonging to user jsmith@corp.local in the Finance department. The initial access vector was a phishing email triggering an encoded PowerShell command from Outlook, leading to the execution of a Cobalt Strike beacon via rundll32 from the Temp directory. The malware established C2 communication over HTTPS to 198.51.100.23, performed host file modification, achieved persistence via a registry run key, and conducted lateral movement via SMB to file server 10.0.3.10. The incident was detected through IDS alerts and EDR process monitoring, but response actions failed due to incorrect targeting. Full containment and eradication were not achieved during the active response phase.

The initial access vector was a phishing email triggering an encoded PowerShell command from Outlook, leading to the execution of a Cobalt Strike beacon via rundll32. The malware established C2 communication with 198.51.100.23 over HTTPS. Evidence of lateral movement was observed via SMB access to 10.0.5.50 and reconnaissance activities including host file modification and Kerberos TGT request attempts. Despite detection by IDS, containment actions (firewall block, endpoint quarantine) were denied due to procedural or policy constraints, indicating a critical gap in incident response authorization protocols.

timeline.description: Initial reconnaissance detected: Nmap SYN scan from 10.0.8.200 targeting 10.0.2.15. Also linked to user CORP\jsmith via source 192.168.1.100.
User CORP\jsmith logs in to WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42).

rundll32.exe loads unsigned beacon.dll from Temp directory, establishing memory-resident payload.
IDS alerts on outbound Cobalt Strike beacon C2 traffic from 10.0.5.42 to 198.51.100.23 over TCP/443.
IDS alerts on suspicious DNS query from 10.0.5.42 to internal DNS server.
Failed Kerberos TGT request from WS-FIN-042, indicating potential credential dumping or brute-force attempt.
Successful SMB access from WS-FIN-042 to file server 10.0.5.50, confirming lateral movement.
Incident formally escalated for ongoing monitoring and post-incident analysis.
